record.paper_title: The Growth Order of a Solution of a Singular Non-Self-Adjoint Differential Equation, as a Function of the Spectral Parameter
record.context_brief: Growth orders of normalized half-line solutions for PT-symmetric Schrödinger equations
record.original_question: For a Schrödinger equation on the real line with a PT-symmetric potential, suppose there are two distinguished solutions ψleft(x, λ) ∈ L²(−∞, 0) and ψright(x, λ) ∈ L²(0, ∞) for the spectral parameter λ; these may be taken as Jost solutions when the potential lies in L¹(ℝ). After normalizing these half-line solutions in an appropriate way, what can be said about their growth orders as functions of λ?

evidence.quote: A similar problem arises in consideration of Schrödinger equations with PT-symmetric potentials on the real line. Here one has two solutions ψleft(x, λ) ∈ L2(−∞, 0) and ψright(x, λ) ∈ L2(0,∞), Jost solutions, for instance, if the potential lies in L1(R).
Normalizing these solutions in some appropriate way, what can one say about their growth orders?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-dimensional Schrödinger equation
$$-\psi''(x) + V(x)\psi(x) = \lambda\,\psi(x), \qquad x\in\mathbb{R},\ \lambda\in\mathbb{C},$$
with a PT-symmetric potential, i.e. a (generally complex-valued) measurable function $V:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{C}$ satisfying $V(-x)=\overline{V(x)}$ for almost every $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Assume $V\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$, so that for every $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}$ with $\operatorname{Im}\sqrt{\lambda}>0$ (taking the branch with non-negative imaginary part) there exist Jost-type solutions: a solution $\psi_{\mathrm{left}}(\cdot,\lambda)$ that is square-integrable on $(-\infty,0)$ and a solution $\psi_{\mathrm{right}}(\cdot,\lambda)$ that is square-integrable on $(0,\infty)$. After fixing a normalization of these half-line solutions (for example, prescribing the asymptotic form $\psi_{\mathrm{right}}(x,\lambda)\sim e^{i\sqrt{\lambda}\,x}$ as $x\to+\infty$ and $\psi_{\mathrm{left}}(x,\lambda)\sim e^{-i\sqrt{\lambda}\,x}$ as $x\to-\infty$, or another comparable normalization), determine the growth order of $\psi_{\mathrm{left}}(x,\lambda)$ and $\psi_{\mathrm{right}}(x,\lambda)$, as well as of relevant connection coefficients between them, regarded as entire (or meromorphic) functions of the spectral parameter $\lambda$. In particular, provide sharp bounds of the form
$$|\psi_{\mathrm{left/right}}(x,\lambda)| \le C(x)\exp\!\big(A(x)|\lambda|^{\rho}\big)$$
identifying the optimal exponent $\rho$ (the order) and, where possible, the type, in terms of the regularity and decay properties of $V$.
artifact.status_search_result: No specific resolution of this question for general PT-symmetric $L^1$ potentials on $\mathbb{R}$ was located in available sources; classical results give order $1/2$ growth for Jost solutions of selfadjoint Schrödinger problems on a half-line, but a definitive PT-symmetric whole-line analogue with sharp growth orders for normalized half-line solutions does not appear to be conclusively settled in the literature reviewed.

status_evidence.title: The Growth Order of a Solution of a Singular Non-Self-Adjoint Differential Equation
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses growth orders of solutions and raises the analogous question for PT-symmetric Schrödinger equations on the real line.
status_evidence.claim: The PT-symmetric whole-line growth-order question is posed but not resolved in the cited work.
